title: Cleaned machine
statement: Given a deterministic Turing machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes, Boolean alphabet, and state set $S$, and an initial state $q_0\in S$, define a machine with $2k$ work tapes and cleaning states. It starts in the initialization state for $q_0$, marks the origin on the added tapes, and then simulates $M$ on the first $k$ tapes while maintaining marks on the added tapes; when $M$ halts, it proceeds through the cleaning phases to erase those marks and return the work tapes to blank, halting after the cleaning process.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a $k$-work-tape Boolean-alphabet machine with state set $S$
caveat: The definition specifies detailed transition behavior; the compressed description may omit operational details such as movement and write choices.
